source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 29: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 29; troubleshooting lens): compare the same checkpoint, tokenizer, prompt/request trace, decoding limits, batcher, serving version, hardware, topology, driver/runtime, power and thermal policy. Change only weight precision; hold activation and KV-cache precision fixed, and record bit width, group size, scale/zero-point method, calibration data, outlier handling, kernel selection, and any fallback. Use an authorized disposable test environment, redact prompts and telemetry, and label measured values versus estimates.

Falsifiable hypothesis and gates: weight-only quantization lowers fully loaded cost per successful output token without violating pre-registered quality, safety, functional-correctness, or latency SLO tolerances. Reject the claim if paired held-out quality/safety or task-correctness scores regress beyond tolerance, error/retry/timeout/OOM rates rise, p95/p99 TTFT or TPOT breaches its budget, throughput fails to improve at matched concurrency, or cost per successful token does not improve. Competing explanations include calibration mismatch, unsupported kernels/fallbacks, batching or arrival-rate changes, and thermal throttling.

Controlled measurement plan: hash and freeze all artifacts and use disjoint calibration, development, and held-out sets. Randomize or interleave repeated baseline and quantized runs over the same request trace; warm up separately, then collect enough repetitions to report paired means/medians and 95% confidence intervals. Measure output quality, safety and functional pass rate; GPU/CPU memory, utilization and power; TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency p50/p95/p99; throughput in requests and tokens per second; concurrency saturation; kernel/fallback counters; errors, retries, timeouts, OOMs, and cleanup state. Compute cost including capacity, energy, calibration, retries, and operational overhead, not parameter bytes alone.

Confounders and rollback: stratify by prompt length, output length, concurrency and hardware; check drift, cache state, scheduling, driver, batch composition and thermal conditions. Do not generalize from one workload or infer causality if kernel selection is unverified. Promote only if every quality/safety/correctness and SLO gate passes with uncertainty reported. Canary the immutable baseline and retain its artifacts; on a gate failure, anomaly, unsafe output, or unbounded resource use, stop the test, route back to the baseline, remove quantized artifacts, and verify routing, caches, permissions and cleanup.
risks: unsupported or fallback kernels may erase cost or latency gains
calibration or held-out distribution mismatch may hide quality and safety regressions
batching, arrival rate, thermal state, driver, or scheduler changes may confound paired results
prompts and telemetry may contain sensitive data
rollback or cleanup may leave artifacts, routing state, or cache state behind
evidence_required: hashed checkpoint, tokenizer, quantization, calibration, kernel, runtime, and serving configurations
disjoint held-out quality, safety, and functional results with paired 95% confidence intervals
request-level latency, throughput, memory, utilization, power, concurrency, error, retry, timeout, OOM, fallback, and cleanup traces
auditable fully loaded cost-per-successful-token calculation and rollback record

Confounders and rollback: stratify by prompt length, output length, concurrency and hardware; check drift, cache state, scheduling, driver, batch composition and thermal conditions. Do not generalize from one workload or infer causality if kernel selection is unverified. Promote only if every quality/safety/correctness and SLO gate passes with uncertainty reported. Canary the immutable baseline and retain its artifacts; on a gate failure, anomaly, unsafe output, or unbounded resource use, stop the test, route back to the baseline, remove quantized artifacts, and verify routing, caches, permissions and cleanup.
risks: unsupported or fallback kernels may erase cost or latency gains
calibration or held-out distribution mismatch may hide quality and safety regressions
batching, arrival rate, thermal state, driver, or scheduler changes may confound paired results
prompts and telemetry may contain sensitive data
rollback or cleanup may leave artifacts, routing state, or cache state behind
evidence_required: hashed checkpoint, tokenizer, quantization, calibration, kernel, runtime, and serving configurations
disjoint held-out quality, safety, and functional results with paired 95% confidence intervals
request-level latency, throughput, memory, utilization, power, concurrency, error, retry, timeout, OOM, fallback, and cleanup traces
auditable fully loaded cost-per-successful-token calculation and rollback record
